incentives.name: Data center sales and use tax exemption
incentives.what: 100% sales tax exemption on data center construction materials and equipment, granted by the Tax Credit Authority. Gov. DeWine ordered the Tax Credit Authority to stop taking new data center requests after its June 1, 2026 meeting while the Joint Data Center Committee studies impacts; existing exemptions unaffected.
incentives.value_known: 2025 cost about $1.6B in state sales tax plus about $446M local (about $2B total; 2024 about $722M). Ohio has agreed to at least $2.3B in state exemptions for 18 companies.

incentives.name: Data center sales tax exemption: history
incentives.what: Enacted in 2016; eliminated in the 2025 budget bill but reinstated (governor's veto).

incentives.name: Data center sales tax exemption: reported investment
incentives.what: DeWine said data centers previously granted sales and use tax benefits reported total capital investment of $27.2B in 2025.
incentives.value_known: $27.2B capital investment (2025), not the cost of the break

incentives.name: Pause on new data center sales tax exemptions
incentives.law: Executive direction to Tax Credit Authority
incentives.what: DeWine froze new data center exemption requests on May 27, 2026.

incentives.name: Local property tax abatements (Community Reinvestment Areas, PILOTs)
incentives.what: Cities grant 15- to 30-year, up to 100% property tax abatements, often with PILOT payments to schools. In New Albany, 17 data centers have 65%-100% abatements over 15 years. Statewide abatement data not available.

dockets.what: AEP Ohio data center tariff. New data centers over 25 MW must pay for at least 85% of contracted demand each month for up to 12 years (incl. 4-year ramp), show financial viability, and pay exit fees if cancelled. Settlement of AEP, PUCO staff, Ohio Consumers' Counsel, Ohio Energy Group, OPAE and Walmart (Oct 23, 2024); a rival data center industry settlement (Google, Amazon, Microsoft etc., 75% minimum) was not adopted. Order lifts AEP's moratorium on new central Ohio data center agreements.
dockets.status: Approved July 9, 2025; data center interests' rehearing request denied (Ohio Capital Journal); OMA Energy Group said it would appeal. Tariff effective July 23, 2025; second load-study tranche: applications due Sept 30, 2026, studies start Oct 1, 2026 (AEP Data Center Tariff page).

dockets.what: AEP Ohio rate case; AEP proposed extending the data center tariff to all data center customers, a $20,000/month supplemental customer charge, and barring existing data centers from the 6CP pilot. PUCO staff recommended approval except the supplemental charge.
dockets.status: Settlement filed Jan 7, 2026 (distribution rates down $58.7M overall, about -$1.22/month for a 1,000 kWh home); PUCO hearing expected Q1 2026; as of Oct 15, 2026 AEP's case page still says rates change only after PUCO approves - no final order found

dockets.what: Apollo Power Generation Facility: 350 MW gas plus about 120 MW batteries on 147 acres in Middleton Township, Wood County, serving only the adjacent Meta data center; approved through expedited review with no public hearings, 34 conditions.
dockets.status: approved; construction set to start Feb 2026

dockets.utility: FirstEnergy (Ohio Edison, Cleveland Electric Illuminating, Toledo Edison)
dockets.what: FirstEnergy data center tariff proceeding; Ohio Consumers' Counsel filed reply comments for consumer protection on Aug 25, 2026. Case number and proposed terms not read (PUCO docket site blocked).

dockets.utility: FirstEnergy (Ohio Edison, Cleveland Electric Illuminating, Toledo Edison)
dockets.what: Distribution rate case filed April 22, 2026: about $800M/yr distribution spending plus $83M/yr tree trimming recovered 2027-2029; typical residential increase about $4.26-$5.30/month each year. OCC factsheet mentions no data center provisions.

Electric distribution rate case: about 38% increase in distribution charges, about +$8.32/month for a typical home, effective 2027 if approved. OCC factsheet mentions no data center provisions. No Duke Energy Ohio large-load or data center tariff docket found in pass 2.
dockets.status: pending; public hearings Dec 1 and Dec 10, 2026

dockets.what: 72.9 MW behind-the-meter natural gas fuel cell facility (228 Bloom Energy units) at 4186 Scioto Darby Creek Rd, Hilliard, serving Amazon's data center campus; AEP builds and owns, Amazon pays. Hilliard appealed the Ohio EPA air permit to ERAC (Nov 2025) and withdrew Sept 15, 2026.
dockets.status: approved, effective Sept 22, 2025; operation projected Sept 2027

dockets.what: Southern Ohio 765 kV transmission for the planned Piketon data center campus: Hanging Rock-Baku line (~33 miles new) and the Baku-Gavin line (to be filed as 26-0426-EL-BTX); customer pays for the transmission; construction late 2027 to 2029.

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 state budget repeal of data center sales tax exemption
laws_and_bills.what: Legislature passed a provision ending the data center sales tax exemption; Gov. DeWine vetoed it; House Speaker Huffman said he lacked the 60 votes to override. Budget bill number not given in source.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 374 (repeal of data center sales tax exemption)
laws_and_bills.what: Bipartisan Senate bill to repeal the exemption (reported effective Oct 1, 2027). Rep. Rader introduced a House companion (reported as HB 975, effective Oct 1, 2026). HB 957 (introduced May 27, 2026) would also bar new exemptions (secondary source only; official legislature site did not load).

laws_and_bills.name: Joint Data Center Committee legislative package
laws_and_bills.what: Would shrink new data center tax breaks (not existing ones). Scheduled vote pulled late June 10, 2026 after House Republicans wanted full repeal.

laws_and_bills.name: Citizen constitutional amendment to ban large data centers
laws_and_bills.what: Rural Ohioans circulating petitions for a November ballot amendment banning data centers over 25 MW statewide; qualification not checked.

local_rules.what: At least 138 municipalities and townships had active data center moratoriums as of Sept 17, 2026; 23 more effectively ban them; at least 23 more considering. A state budget amendment limits community referendums on zoning for megaproject property.
No zoning permits for data centers; zoning standards being drafted.
One-year moratorium on all data centers on unincorporated land, unanimous trustee vote May 2026.
Data center moratorium approved earlier in 2026.
Moratorium (C-22-26); Project Maple 310-acre data center plan on hold subject to it.
12-month moratorium on new data centers passed 6-1.
Data center moratorium until early November 2026, blocking the Bitdeer proposal until it ends.
12-month pause on new data center planning applications after residents objected to a Pacifico Energy data center and power plant.
City paused new data centers while local impacts are studied.
Ward 15 Councilman Charles Slife introduced a data center moratorium ordinance May 4, 2026.
One-year moratorium on data centers while the village sets zoning rules; hits the McDonald Steel site project (Oppidan Connect).

18-month moratorium on new data center construction (July 2026) after June 2026 rules limiting data centers to industrial zones and denying AI data center permits; subcommittee to report Oct 20, 2026.
Data center zoning rules: 10,000 gallons/day water cap, 40-decibel noise limit, 10 MW maximum facility load, air-cooled only, decommissioning plan with bond; PUD exemption added.
Data centers made a conditional use in 2024 (needs added review and approval).
